questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of renaming branches?
options: Renaming a local branch changes its local reference name; remote branch names and upstream tracking relationships must be considered separately. Communicate changes when teammates or automation rely on the old name.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Renaming a local branch changes its local reference name; remote branch names and upstream tracking relationships must be considered separately. Communicate changes when teammates or automation rely on the old name.
questions.explanation: Renaming a local branch changes its local reference name; remote branch names and upstream tracking relationships must be considered separately. Communicate changes when teammates or automation rely on the old name.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git branch -m feature/renamed-example` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with renaming branches?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
